first_public_basis: bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2020.06.30.180935 v1, posted 2020-07-01 (single version; phoneme classification and both confound analyses; no speech synthesis). Journal version (J Neural Eng 17(6):066007, online 2020-11-11) adds Brain-to-Speech synthesis. Wiki text = PMC author manuscript of the journal version.
setting: Decoders of produced, attempted or imagined speech from human intracranial recordings (ECoG, sEEG, depth electrodes, intracortical arrays), one population for M06 and M12: ledger-pattern studies first public before 2020-01, filtered by title and ledger text to actual decoders (reviews, perception or listening studies, mapping or encoding analyses, non-speech BCIs removed), versions merged. 2020-01 to 2021-01 is [concurrent]. Absence claims are also checked by a whole-wiki full-text pattern over any signal.

M01.lineage: Stavisky et al. 2019: visually prompted overt speaking by BrainGate2 participants

M02.lineage: audio-derived phoneme labels and onsets; no training-only signal

M03.lineage: per-participant supervised fit within folds; RNN noise and drift augmentation from Willett et al. handwriting work

M04.lineage: overt speech by participants able to speak (Stavisky et al. 2019)

M05.lineage: two 96-electrode Utah arrays in dorsal hand-knob area, same participant T5 and arrays as Stavisky et al. 2019; HLFP and threshold crossings

topics.inclusion_rule: Published rule (intracranial signal named with phonemes, vowels, consonants or syllables in the ledger text; design = size of the speech-unit class set). For this target the decoder population of the plan setting, first public before 2020-01; design regexes of the published table applied as mention counts; the deciding priors (full-inventory and deep-network intracranial classifiers) read in full. Boundary: synthesis-only decoders stay in the population but are not class-set designs; versions merged.

M07.lineage: no language model; closed 420-word prompt set

M08.lineage: phoneme class label; Brain-to-Speech unit-selection synthesis of Herff et al. 2019 (journal version only)

topics.inclusion_rule: Same decoder population as M06 (plan setting, first public before 2020-01). Design of interest: an explicit control for overt-speech confounds in the evaluation: an audio-neural contamination test or artifact removal, decoding from a window before voice onset, or neural rather than acoustic onset alignment. Boundary: a confound named only in related work or in the reference list does not count; full-text pattern counts are mention counts; assessment studies without a decoder (Roussel et al.) are read as deciding priors but not counted as decoders; whole-wiki full-text pattern for contamination terms over any signal.
topics.metric: decoding accuracy change after contamination control
